subject: Re: Proposed evaluation milestones, ramp schedule, and true-up mechanics
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed MAP and redlines for evaluation to commit

Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Attached is a one-page MAP and our initial redlines on economics (see 'Acme-Redlines.docx' attached). High-level asks:

- We want a 90-day evaluation with a staged commit if metrics are met (see milestones tab).
- Pricing must include a 6-month price-protection window after the initial committed term.
- True-ups: we prefer quarterly reconciliations rather than monthly.
- Definitions: we propose language that caps billable tokens to 'inference tokens' excluding internal test traffic.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate a quarterly true-up and a 6-month price protection? Also attaching the MAP spreadsheet so you can align on dates.

Alex
Procurement, Acme Corp
Attachment: 20260820-Acme-MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), Acme-Redlines.docx (doc)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposed MAP and redlines for evaluation to commit

Team — forwarding Acme's MAP and redlines. Key negotiation points they flagged: quarterly true-ups, 6-month price protection post-term, and a restrictive "billable tokens" def that excludes internal test traffic.

Quick notes / asks:
- Neha: can legal sign off on quarterly true-ups and the proposed definition for billable tokens? Any concerns with ambiguity?
- Marcus: what impact does a 6-month price-protection window have on our revenue model for a staged commit with an aggressive ramp? I'd like a short sensitivity: best/worst case ARR impact if pricing is locked for 6 months.
- Laura: will want to align CS success milestones to the MAP's rollout dates; are the milestones achievable with our default onboarding plan?

I propose we respond with a counter that accepts quarterly true-ups, proposes a 3-month price-protection window (instead of 6), and clarifies the billable token definition to exclude lab/test traffic under a specific filtering tag (so we can audit).

Please reply with redline language snippets by EOD tomorrow.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed MAP and redlines for evaluation to commit

Hannah / team — read through Acme's redlines. Preliminary legal guidance:

- Quarterly true-ups: acceptable. We should explicitly state the reconciliation date (e.g., end of calendar quarter) and the window for dispute (30 days).
- Price-protection: 6 months is on the long side. Counter to 3 months is defensible; alternatively, we can offer 6 months but only at a step-down protection (e.g., protection applies to the initial committed SKU only, not add-ons or newly onboarded features).
- Billable tokens definition: we cannot accept an open-ended exclusion. Proposed language: "Billable Tokens: tokens generated from requests that reach Redwood production endpoints, excluding calls tagged with the customer-managed 'test' header and IP ranges declared in Schedule A. Redwood reserves the right to audit and reject credits for traffic that appears artificially excluded."
- True-up mechanics: state that usage above commitment is invoiced at list price in the quarter, with any contract-level discounts applied on the subsequent invoice upon reconciliation. Also include a single-sentence SLA that performance regressions do not constitute grounds for retroactive refunds.

I'll draft precise redline snippets and upload. If Sales wants to trade a longer price-protection for a ramp commit guarantee (e.g., 3-month ramp to 50% of committed capacity), that could be a negotiating lever.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP and redlines for evaluation to commit

Alex — thanks for the clarity and the MAP. We reviewed the redlines internally and propose the following counterpoints (high level):

1) True-ups: Redwood can accept quarterly reconciliations with invoices issued on the following month's invoice cycle. Reconciliation disputes must be raised within 30 days of receipt.

2) Price protection: we cannot offer an open 6-month hard lock at the standard committed discount. We can do a 3-month price-protection window for the committed SKUs at the agreed discount. In exchange: we ask for a staged ramp commitment that reaches 60% of the committed QPS within 90 days of go-live.

3) Billable tokens: we agree to exclude clearly-tagged lab/test traffic. Proposed implementable language: calls sent with header 'X-Acme-Test: true' or originating from IPs listed in Schedule A will be excluded from billable usage; Redwood will include audit logs for excluded traffic at the quarterly reconciliation.

I've attached a countersheet with milestone dates (20260822-Redwood-Counter-Milestones.xlsx). If acceptable, we can map these milestones into a short SOW and lock dates in DocuSign.

Proposed next step: confirm whether Acme can accept the 3-month protection in exchange for the ramp commitment. If so we'll circulate a single-page SOW and updated redlines.

Best,
Hannah
Attachment: 20260822-Redwood-Counter-Milestones.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com, Emily Park <emily.park@acme-legal.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 11:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP and redlines for evaluation to commit

Hannah — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of clarifications from our side after talking to Product and Legal: 

- Quarterly true-ups: fine.
- Price protection: 6 months is important to our CFO. We can accept a trade: Acme will commit to the 60% ramp to committed QPS within 90 days and will provide quarterly visibility calls with Redwood's CS team. In return, we need a 6-month protection on base committed SKU pricing. If Redwood is unwilling to provide a full 6 months, would Redwood consider 6 months with a staged protection: months 1–3 full protection, months 4–6 at 50% of the original protection (i.e., partial protection)?
- Billable token tagging: Product prefers token exclusion based on an internal 'test' header; they asked if Redwood can provide a short guide on how to instrument that and how audit logs will look during reconciliation.

We are fine with the staged ramp and will sign a one-page SOW if we can agree on the protection mechanics. Also attaching our redlines doc with minor cleanup: 20260824-Acme-Redlines.docx.

—Alex

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP and redlines for evaluation to commit

Alex — good, sounds like we're close. Final proposal from Redwood:

- True-ups: quarterly reconciliations, invoice adjustment on the next billing cycle, 30-day dispute window.
- Price protection: staged protection accepted: months 1–3 full protection on the committed SKU; months 4–6 protection at 50% (i.e., we reserve the right to adjust pricing thereafter). We will include explicit language that add-ons and new feature SKUs are excluded from the protection.
- Ramp: Acme to achieve 60% of committed QPS within 90 days. If Acme misses ramp milestones, Redwood may pause protection benefits on a forward-looking basis after a 30-day cure period.
- Billable tokens: include the 'X-Acme-Test: true' header exclusion + IP ranges declared in Schedule A; Redwood will provide a template instrument guide and sample audit CSV for reconciliation.

Next steps: I'll put the negotiated bullets into a 1-page SOW and route for acceptance and DocuSign. Marcus, Laura — can you confirm the ramp checklist and CS resources so I can attach to the SOW? Neha, I'll send the redline snippet for the staged protection clause by EOD.

Thanks — almost there.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
